stem: Bluegrain Media expects sudden read spikes on a new DynamoDB table and wants minimal preplanning while avoiding throttling from mode-switching mistakes.

choices.text: Use provisioned mode only because on-demand cannot scale beyond prior peaks.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams shards as the table throughput billing control.
Use Aurora provisioned instances and manually tune DynamoDB demand windows each week to bypass table mode limits.
Use on-demand mode and remember provisioned-to-on-demand switching is limited to four times per 24 hours.

rationale: On-demand suits unpredictable spikes and scales to prior and new peaks, while the switching-limit fact prevents incorrect operational assumptions. Provisioned mode alone increases planning burden for this requirement. Aurora pricing controls are different from DynamoDB capacity modes. Kinesis shards are streaming units, not DynamoDB table throughput modes.
